Generate checks from your form, then add custom rules for requirements the form cannot express.

## 1. Generate field and structure rules

This example copies the bundled survey into a temporary directory:

```{r}
library(form.validation)
directory <- tempfile("survey-rules-")
dir.create(directory)
file.copy(form.model::form_resource("examples/survey-form.yaml", "form.model"), directory)
generate_validation_rules("survey", directory, version = "1")
```

For your own form, use its name and directory. Regenerate after changing the definition, using `overwrite = TRUE`.

## 2. Add a custom rule

The bundled business rule warns when the total observation count exceeds its configured maximum:

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
examples <- system.file("examples", package = "form.validation")
cat("```yaml\n", paste(readLines(file.path(examples, "survey-business-validation.yaml")), collapse="\n"), "\n```\n", sep="")
```

Its callback returns a finding when the total is too high:

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat("```r\n", paste(readLines(file.path(examples, "business.R")), collapse="\n"), "\n```\n", sep="")
```

Return `NULL` when the check passes. Use `validation_incomplete()` when required information is unavailable.

## 3. Declare the process

The process lists the generated files followed by your business rules:

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat("```yaml\n", paste(readLines(file.path(examples, "survey-validation.yaml")), collapse="\n"), "\n```\n", sep="")
```

All files must identify the same model and rules version. Regeneration preserves your business file.
